summary: Fixed R-15: test/access.test.js now renders the empty-shelf page through a second real server and runs the same A3 structure checks on it. No production change was needed. The full suite passes (84/84).

experiments.name: access tests with the new empty-shelf test

mutation: src/pages.js empty-shelf

replaced with an

and an unlabelled input; the new empty-shelf test fails (6 pass, 1 fail); pages.js then restored

notes: I moved the per-page markup assertions into a checkPage() helper. The existing every-page test calls it for each page, so those assertions are unchanged.
A start(dataPath) helper now spawns the server on a free port. The shared server uses it, and the new test uses it for a temporary file holding {"books":[]} so the other pages' data is untouched.

The new test checks status 200 and the title 'The Oak Street shelf'. It also checks the 'The shelf is empty right now.' message in <main>, and that the page has no book list and no refusal block, so a wrong branch cannot pass.

The mutation was the one described in the finding's evidence: a skipped heading level plus an unlabelled input in place of the empty-shelf paragraph. It turned only the new test red, and pages.js is restored with no diff.

I did not take up the second note, that rule() only sees the first rule for a selector. A later overriding rule would not turn T-29 or the A2 checks red. That is a limit of the regression guard and does not fail A4.

The A1/A2 browser findings from earlier rounds stand, and the gate's wider run (every page, keyboard walk) supersedes them. The hand lettering still cannot be seen in this environment's Chromium; I make no V-11 lettering claim.
